text_fidelity_a:
Zune HD 32 GB Video MP3 Player (Platinum) For the past 5 years or so, I've been rocking it out to a Sandisk Sansa. Those were nice little MP3 players, that in my opinion, were superior to the iPod. Well, the Age of the Touch Screen is here, and I wanted an upgrade. The Zune HD seemed like the only solid choice, if I wanted to avoid loading iTunes onto my computer. So I bought one. So far, I think it's a neat little device that gives me *most* of what I want. The sound quality is great, and I like having the internet in my pocket. Microsoft did a fine job with the OS and software; I've had no problems figuring it out. For web capability, it's a bit small, but then again, I appreciate it's size as an MP3 player. I also really like the touch screen. It's nice and responsive, so no problems there, either. Now here's a list of things I'd like to see:

*Micro SD Card slot
*Google Apps
*Netflix (It supports HD vid, so why not Netflix?!)
*Some sort of email client
*Non-proprietary cable for charging.

So far, Microsoft has done a decent job. I'd give it a B+, and I would also feel good about recommending the device to my friends and family.
text_fidelity_b: Zune HD 32 GB Video MP3 Player (Platinum)

text_fidelity_a:
Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10 Noise Isolating Earphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This was one of the last Ultimate Ears earbud lines before Logitech bought the company which resulted in an immediate drop in product quality and increase in product price. Yes, these are still wired headphones, but the sound fidelity is unmatched, and instead of complicated noise cancelling algorithms this simply employs noise isolation to block out ambient sound. These headphones have been out of production for some time, but for whatever reason you can still find them NIB from many vendors. They charge about a little more than what cut-rate vendors charged when they were new about 6 years ago, but they were way ahead of their time and frankly nothing on the market in this price range sounds even close to this good. Plus, these original UE headphones (I don't evangelize anything UE after Logitech bought them) have a lot of great design features. The earbud units are modular, so if you ever destroy the leads, you can always replace them for $10. Also, the standard leads these ship with do NOT have the mic and volume/start-stop control on the leads, but you can buy them in various levels of quality for about $20-60 aftermarket and swap them out. It's money well spent if you want to make calls on them. Also, the lead up to 6" from each bud is cased in memory metal so they can be bent to shape and hold in place to are a comfy fit on he outside of your ears- great idea.

All around the best earbud headphones for the money, if you can find them!
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10 Noise Isolating Earphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd) I bought this tablet as a gift for my mom for x-mas. Although my wife and I have been *very* happy with our Apple iPad, I couldn't bring myself to spend $499 for a gift that I wasn't even sure my mom was going to use. In retrospect, I should have spent the extra money.

On the surface, the Kindle Fire HD 8.9" has a lot going for it: great speakers (but not really loud enough!), excellent wi-fi reception, and a screen that is very nice, indeed. In general (more on that later), performance is good also and overall build quality seems excellent - I'd say on par with the iPad.

So what is the problem?

Well, it all boils down to poor usability. At least for people who are not technologically inclined or those who don't have good hand/eye coordination. Let me explain by way of my experiences trying to teach my mom how to use the device:

The first stumbling block for my mom was finding the power and volume buttons. They are the same black color as the tablet and don't stick out much. They are difficult, especially with pudgy fingers, to find easily.

The second problem involves a GUI principle known as "discoverability". Quite a few very common functions on the Fire HD are not visible at all - the user has to simply "know" the gesture that brings them forth. The primary example I speak of is the "Settings" & brightness adjustment. You'd think that something like "Settings" would deserve a button somewhere on the user interface, but the Amazon GUI designers didn't think so. They thought that it is instinctively intuitive to swipe down from the top of the screen to expose a menu that has a brightness slider and something mysteriously labeled "More..." - well, that "More..." turns out to be the "Settings". And, no, my mom did not instinctively know where to swipe to get to these primary functions.

The next problem involves the tablet's lack of flexibility in terms of catering to the visually- or motor-impaired. My mom had a stroke a year ago and although she's fine, her hand-eye coordination is slightly impaired. Enough so, that she had a lot of trouble with two primary navigation icons on the Fire HD: the "Home" (picture of a house) and "Back" (a left arrow) buttons. These buttons are quite small and very close to one another. My mom, unless she was very careful, would sometimes hit one versus the other. Unlike the iPad, the Amazon Fire HD has ABSOLUTELY NO ACCESSIBILTY settings to help out with this sort of thing. Common, Amazon, there was absolutely no reason to make those icons so small AND so close to one another. That's just stupid UI design (I know whereof I speak - I'm a GUI software developer).

Then we ran into the problem of the tablet getting slower over time - the carousels that Amazon was so fond of and designed a whole GUI with them no longer moved smoothly; menus took a second or two to popup, pages on books no longer flipped effortlessly. I suspected an app we had started was causing a problem (I think it was Skype), but I had the hardest time finding the place to kill running applications. I don't remember exactly how long it took, but it must have been 10-20 minutes. It shouldn't be that hard to kill off running applications! By contrast, on all iOS devices, you get to your running apps by double-tapping the Home button. Maybe Android has a standard too, but since Amazon completely "redesigned" the user interface of Android, that wouldn't have mattered.

Finally, there are the applications - or, should I say, the lack of applications. Amazon does not let its Fire HD users access the Google Play store and its hundreds of thousands of apps. Instead, they get the Amazon store - with not many of the most useful apps. Most notably, I did not see any replacement browsers for the horribly slow one that Amazon put on its Fire tablets ("Silk" is anything but silky smooth). I don't even recall finding Google apps (but I have to admit to not having spent a lot of time in the Amazon store, searching).

All, in all, I think the Amazon Fire HD 8.9" is a pretty limited device for a limited set of users. It is nowhere near as functional and as useful as an iPad. I hate to say it, given how much a fan of Amazon and the Kindle e-readers I am, but I wish I had not been so cheap and gotten my parents an iPad. There is a reason those tablets are becoming the defacto standard in schools, rehabilitation centers, etc. They're fool proof and have a GUI anybody can understand.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire HD 8.9", 8.9" HD display, 16 GB or 32 GB, Wi-Fi or Optional 4G LTE Wireless (Previous Generation - 2nd)

JVC HARX700 Precision Sound Full Size Headphones - Black ~Comfortable for hours. These are light years ahead of earbuds, on ear, or over ear phones. No part of my ear was pinched or scrunched, even though I wear glasses. I have an over-sized melon and large, flat ears. I can't tolerate buds for more than about 30 minutes, and most headphones in this range are pinchy somewhere.
~I normally watch movies/videos at full sound with Closed Caption on iPad or laptops. I'm at half volume -- no CC -- wearing these phones. I was able to easily pick up male and female voices, including foreign accents.
~NOT noise cancelling. I could still hear the whir of a fan, my kids talking, etc., but they couldn't hear any noise coming from my headphones. For me, this was ideal. I don't have the luxury of tuning out the world most of the time.
~Requires several hours of break-in. I usually listen to Winterspell from Two Steps to test buds and phones. It sounded tinny on first listen, and amazing about 10 hours in.
I highly recommend these if you have moderate hearing loss. I can't differentiate consonant sounds, and certain voices and accents are nearly impossible for me to follow on screen. These didn't feel loud, just incredibly clear -- it was like hearing like a kid again.

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130) Arlo is not perfect, but it is wicked close.

What's Great: You can put it anywhere within range of the link/router. The alerts are reliable, if a little slow on the uptake. The picture is good. Set up was simple and worked the first time. A reasonable amount of cloud storage is free, and it's easy to download whatever you want to save. The cameras are easy to move around to wherever you need them, and you don't have to set them up again.

What's Okay: A person who walks fast can get through a room almost faster than Arlo can start recording. Now, it's still much faster than an old Belkin Netcam HD, which sends pictures of where the motion WAS. Before the picture. And the D-Link 930L, which is a fine monitor cam, but has never been able to send a snap or a clip, no matter how many times it has been set up to do that. However, both of those cameras have audio and stream reasonably good images via their apps (the Belkin video resolution is way better than the Dlink). That makes them okay monitors next to smart security sensors - if the sensor alerts, you can look to see what tripped it and listen to see what's going on. Arlo will - most of the time - catch whatever set it off and let you know within seconds. And it's free, not an extra $$$ feature.

What Could Be Better: The link thing is enormous. It could be a little less expensive. And it would be WONDERFUL if it integrated with Z-Wave or Smart Things. The plan here is to station the Arlo cams near other devices that send push notifications - Nest Alarms, Smanos smart sensors, etc.

How It Compares: Beats the Canary I couldn't get to activate. Way better than the other netcams in the house. Love it. Just added another camera.
text_fidelity_b: Arlo - Wireless Home Security | Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, Wall Mount | Includes Cloud Storage & Required Base Station | 1-Camera System (VMS3130)

If you are simply expecting these to hold things together reasonably well, then they are perfectly adequate for the task. However, when I tested them by tying them to weights and using them to lift, I found that they broke about 1/2 the time at 30 pounds, never quite reaching 40 pounds.

They are reliably good for 20 pounds without breaking, which is not too bad, really, for something so small. While I feel that the 40 pound claim is somewhat misleading, they are actually comparable to most similar sized ties on the market as far as I can tell, and it's doubtful that most others would perform any better. If you're not using them to lift heavy weights then they'll work just fine, and you'd be hard pressed to find a better price for this quantity of similar ties.

Once you remove the back openings for PCIe cards, they are gone. You can't reinstall if you decide to change the configuration. So then you need to get the covers.
The case fan can be a little noisy - part of this is solvable by moving the cords out of the way so they don't vibrate. The cords come out of the top of the fan instead of the bottom, so gravity causes them to lay against it which makes noise.

This may be a plus or minus, depending on what you like:
The Lights. The lights will light up a dark room. This is made worse/better by the clear side (that shows all your messy cords if you don't make them look all nice.) where the blue and red lights glow out of. Mine is currently still in the open room, as I am waiting for more RAM and loading programs. When it is all set up it will be under a desk and maybe not so noticeable when on. Though I guess if it is in your room it would be like a night light. :)

text_fidelity_a:
Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple) [[VIDEOID:e832f455c8dfddb522ae3bbc1ec73698]] Loved the idea of an underwater camera for kids, and this one would have been great if not for the terrible image quality that would only disappoint any except maybe youngest of kids.

When I unpacked the box, I had great expectations. The waterproof shell seemed to be solid and to seal well, and there was a whole lot of extra parts to attach the camera to a bicycle and so on. Camera is very small, but the little screen is bright and it shows the image you're taking clearly. The interface is intuitive and reasonably simple. (I didn't bother to set the date before trying out the camera, but the instructions were clear, and I was able to test it with no problem, it works.)

HOWEVER: I can't believe how bad quality of the images are! They look jagged and pixelated like they're at 480 pixels. Even when I increased the quality in the settings to maximum image resolution, which is supposed to be 20Mb and 7344 pixels (more than what I shoot at for my professional photography biz), the quality stayed the same and the file size only crept up to just below 1 Meg. No idea how they managed to accomplish that. Their image sensor is at about the quality of those blurry, pixelated security cameras that are completely useless for identification. Otherwise, this camera focuses surprisingly well and handles a wide range of light conditions automatically. All the images were in a good range.

The video was marginally better, but still not what you'd expect at 1080 resolution. Camera was recognized by my Windows laptop right away, and I was able to access and copy images with no problem.

It's such a shame that the manufacturer decided to save money on image quality and it's a weird business decision that makes an otherwise fun and well built product useless.

Photos above were taken by the reviewed camera:
- The instruction manual image at highest resolution, and you can see its file size in the second screenshot image. Taken without the waterproof case.
- First Batman toy image at default resolution, without waterproof case
-Second Batman toy image at default resolution, with waterproof case on. Surprisingly, not much difference. Good plastic.
text_fidelity_b: Aileho Kids Waterproof Camera Best Pool Toy for Children Birthday Gifts 1080P Kid Digital Underwater Camcorder Sports Action Cam 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 Year Girls 32G SD Card (Dark Purple)

TCL 65" Class 4-Series 4K UHD HDR Roku 2017 Smart TV - 65S405 Do not be afraid! This is a great TV.

The good: I won't go into the technical details and explanations. Others have done that for me. We purchased this for a new home and have had it set up for a couple of weeks. The integration of Roku is seamless, and it retains those same intuitive menus. It has no WiFi connectivity issues for us (we have a Google mesh network with a good signal at the TV location), and effortlessly streams Netflix, Amazon Video and You TubeTV-- DVR and live-- and looks great doing it. I haven't tried 4K content yet, so can't comment on that.

The bad: It doesn't handle low light scenes very well in movies and television, and particularly when viewed from any angle that isn't straight on. That's why I gave it four stars instead of five. If you can overcome that, forge ahead! I couldn't justify spending twice or more on Samsung or others. Another minor quibble-- silver feet on a black frame looks a little odd.

The bottom line: I was skeptical. I've owned Samsung plasma and LED and an LG LED recently and I see no material difference between the TCL and the other LEDs. All the positive reviews here, plus the CNet reviews/primers on Roku integrated TVs put me over the edge. We really like this TV and it's simplified our streaming incredibly. Go get it!

Garmin vívofit 2 Activity Tracker, White The circumference of my wrist is 5 1/4 inches above the bone which is fairly small and the small wristband fits perfectly, there are still 5 holes (1.5 inches) left to make it smaller.

The two reasons I went for this activity tracker are it is waterproof and the battery lasts one year... for me these are the most important reasons because I really hate all this constant charging of gadgets.

Syncing is easy, at the end of the day I just press one button and it syncs with my smartphone, it also comes with a little blue-tooth USB attachment if you want to sync it with your computer. I've read they will add autosync with the next software update which is supposed to arrive shortly.

You get to choose what to see on your screen when you press the button, I went with steps, goal, distance and time. You can also add the date, calories and heart rate if you are wearing a strap.

I absolutely love how it feels, it doesn't bother me at all, you don't have to wear it real tight and the silicon is very soft.

The reason I took one star off is that the beep sound which comes on after one hour of inactivity (when the red warning line appears) is way, way, way too quiet. I set an alarm just to check on the beep sound and it was so short and subtle, if there would be any kind of background noise you won't be able to hear it at all.

text_fidelity_a: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone - Matte Black (Old Model) These headphones do have a more balanced sound than the horrible original Beats that were just too bass heavy. The Bluetooth pairing was quick and easy and battery life is decent. The case and accessories seem to be good quality. In all honesty though for the sound quality I'd never pay the retail asking price for these or recommend them to anyone. I got a used pair (yes they are real Beats) for half the price of new and at this price point I feel it's worth it. The noise canceling isn't anything to write home about and if it's a big reason why you're considering these I'd look to Bose or elsewhere where it's done much better. Another point with these is comfort. They're ok for an hour or so, but I'd not want these on pushing two or more. They tend to pinch at the ear cup level and you can see in various pics how the cups nearly touch when not on the head. So the farther you are pushing those cups out the more they are fighting to close so to speak. I don't have a large head, I don't expand the headband at all when wearing, and they get a little clampy after a bit. Another comfort issue is the interior depth of the ear cups. I don't have big ear or ones that stick out and I still feel my ears slightly pushing against the speaker. I couldn't imagine anyone with large ears being happy with these at all and if you fall into that category I'd definitely try on a pair in a store before buying. The cup pads are nice and it's too bad they didn't make them just a tad deeper.  So in summary these are good headphones if not great ones, but honestly not worth retail. The Bluetooth is nice, but you're obviously paying for image here.
text_fidelity_b: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone - Matte Black (Old Model)

Kensington Orbit® Fusion™ Wireless Trackball (K72363WW), Black I used a Logitech M570, a thumb trackball, for years until I started gaming again and needed a gaming mouse. Now I’m done with gaming for a while and have been searching for a trackball to reduce strain.

The Kensington Orbit Fusion Wireless Trackball is the first Kensington trackball I’ve tried.

I hate the scroll ring. I think this is either a feature you love or hate, and well, I just don’t like it. Using the scroll ring is uncomfortable for me; I keep going back to my laptop trackpad instead of using it. It’s too easy to move the trackball while using the scroll ring, and I couldn’t decide which finger was most comfortable for using it. I spent a lot of time fiddling with the scrolling speed in the KensingtonWorks program, but content doesn’t move smoothly on my screen -- it jumps.

The mouse is too big for my hand. I usually wear a size small in women’s winter and nitrile gloves, to give an idea of the size. My fingers have to stretch too much to reach the left and right click buttons at the same time. My hand rises off the mouse when I use the scroll ring.

I know some of this is muscle memory, but my wrist and hand actually hurt after using the trackball for more than a few minutes.

I do like that KensingtonWorks can be used on Windows or Mac. I’ve tried a lot of high end gaming mice that I can’t always customize on my Mac. KensingtonWorks lets you modify the pointer, scroll ring, and customize the buttons. You can also back up your settings to Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive, and set options for specific programs. Kensington also included a USB-A to USB-C adapter.
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit® Fusion™ Wireless Trackball (K72363WW), Black

Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter This seemed to be the perfect solution to a problem I was having with obtaining Internet access in my basement. The router is located on the upper floor of the house and, while access is fine in every room above ground, access in the basement has been minimal at best.

Installation was very straightforward - just plug one adapter into the router, the other into the wall socket, and plug in whatever device needs access into one of the three plugs located on the wall socket device.

Overall it works pretty well, but is highly sensitive to noise or heavy draws on the power line. For example, I have a dehumidifier in the basement. When that kicks on, I lose the connection. Sometimes it is regained all by itself, but most of the time I have to either reboot (or power cycle) the device that is plugged in, or unplug and then re-plug the adapter. I tried moving the dehumidifier to a different circuit than the one used by the powerline adapter, and also tried plugging the dehumidifier into a surge protector - no difference. So, I make sure the dehumidifier is off before I use any Internet device.

I've had the same issue with other appliances such as certain vacuums - turn them on, and the connection is lost. There have been no problems with appliances operating in other areas of the house, such as the microwave, laser printers, etc. Just happens when you use the appliance in the same room as the powerline adapter.

But, other than these powerline induced interruptions, the device works well. Speedy connection - can't tell any difference between this and any other WiFi connected device. Well worth taking a look at if you have some WiFi dead zones in your house. Just keep an eye out for someone who is about to use a vacuum when you're at a critical spot in the movie you're streaming!
text_fidelity_b: Belkin VideoLink 3 Powerline Internet Adapter

Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000 Though I have a laptop, I decided to use this solid-state drive as a boot drive on my desktop computer. If you are unfamiliar with the difference between a solid-state and a regular hard drive, the solid-state has no moving parts, which makes it silent, fast, reliable, and shock resistant. It has twice the capacity and twice the speed of the solid-state drive I got a couple of years ago for the same price, and blows away a standard drive for speed.

Given the silence and speed, it makes a great boot drive for running Windows, Photoshop, and other programs where speed is a huge advantage. Just to give you an idea, when upgrading from a regular two-year-old hard drive to this solid-state drive, my Windows boot time went from two minutes to about 10 seconds. Seriously, my computer now starts up and is ready to use in like 10 seconds.

What I do is use a solid-state drive as my boot drive and a regular hard drive as a storage drive. Solid-state drives like this are really expensive to purchase if you need any kind of capacity, but a 200 GB drive will certainly hold all of your programs and often used files.

As for this drive specifically, I hooked it up to my desktop and it was immediately recognized by Windows. The drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up as a drive and work in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

As I said, it's a lot faster than the solid-state drive I had from a couple years ago, and there's no problem using it on my desktop machine rather than my laptop.
text_fidelity_b: Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000

LG Electronics 70UK6570 70-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2018 Model) I bought this set for 4k gaming (PS4 PRO) and 4k films. Anything else like voice integration with google assistant was just a bonus that adds to the overall purchases and very happy with it.

The 70/75 inch model the only major difference is screen panel type. 75 is direct lit and 70 is edge lit. Features pretty much the same.

Out of the box the image using home mode was basic due the fact that all 4k TVs are set to automatic light detection and shifts the image to 'energy saver' slightly dimming them. Just go into the menu settings, picture setting and shut energy saving mode off. This is how all major tvs are shipped inbox. Its not a defect item. After shutting that off, the image settings work like normal. Vivid, sports, cinema etc they also have a professional tv set up for light and dark room. In case you want to hire someone professionally.

HDR effect is simulated HDR on SD content. Also a separate setting for HDR called: HDMI DEEP COLOR in 'additional picture settings' same location. They also have an option for eye strain, if its set on, shut it off. Its used for people who have eye strain from bright sets. I would keep HDMI DEEP COLOR ON to test that your HDMI is working with the TV, it will automatically turn on when it detects a blue-ray disk player with HDR or gaming system using it. Leaving it on, lets you know if the HDMI is compatible with it. Even if you're not using something with HDR. If the HDMI cant pass the signal, it will default to black screen 'no image detected'. In that case shut it off, and get a new HDMI.

After shutting off power saving modes, the tv works perfectly. Vivid images, sharp, major detail and awesome color. Whites are super white, but wont bleed over each other. Reds are blood red and blacks are dark. Everything pops off the screen, keep in mind i'm coming from a 1rst gen 4k tv that lacked a full HDR panel (10 bit). Slow remote response and lacking features that this set has. THIS new set fixes all that.. The blue tooth remote is responsive, fast and almost no lag, feel snappy and responsive. You can also download the LG app and use it as a pointer (like a mouse pointer on a computer). Easiest way to input information like passwords, email etc vs dialing them in on the remote. It can also be used as a pointer to navigate menu settings on screen with click being enter command.

LG has an app store, but haven't had a chance to play around with it. They give out free screensavers images in 4k, fireplace, beach etc and some basic games. In the future, i'll download wallpapers since my gaming is done on the PS4. They also have free apps for TV viewing from online channels. The set comes pre installed with Hulu, Netflix (controller has Netflix button), YouTube, google pictures etc you can also download free online shows that stream for free. From what I read online, Netflix is tuned to the TV for best viewing.

The set also has an update feature for firmware (under about TV settings sections) and you can set it to auto update. Once registered with LG, can also be done from TV. It allows you to use Google Assistance with a few prompts for basic set up. To fully use LG AI thinQ voice built in, you have to get a magic remote (under $50 bucks) and will be buying one soon, since I use voice features a lot. From google assistant from your phone, you can do basics, volume up +5, shut living room TV off and a few other commands that go threw google assistant (phone or google home) . The magic remote uses more the voice feature and you dont have to say: okay google, tell LG to turn off living room TV" saves you a step and allows you to use it for suggestions and what you see in the demo videos. Remember that AI ThinQ is working with Google assistant for results. Not a gimped voice feature like first generation 4k TVs.

My games look phenomenal, brand new including 4k films. Everything seems to have gotten a new coat of paint. The HDR really makes a difference in films and games. These set use HDR10 and HLG (Hybrid log gamma). The only thing it does not do is Dolby Vision. Its a Dolby version of HDR basically. Which to me isn't a deal breaker since HDR10 is more supported in films, streams etc

TV also supports fast wireless connection (wireless AC).

I have nothing negative to say about the set. Had an HDMI/HDR error and that was due to my HDMI not being high speed aka 'premium HDMI'. If you run into a similar issue with PS4 PRO, XBOX X or Blu-ray player. Connect directly to set should fix the issue and see if its the HDMI. Sometimes, like in my case, its an older HDMI that I had going from my sound system out to the LG TV. The PS4 was high speed/premium but the 2nd connection to the TV wasn't, so the chain was broken. Supported 4k but lacked bandwidth with 4k+ HDR.

This set has all major functions
VA panel
Wide Color Gamut (WCG)
4K Ultra HD Resolution
4K Active HDR
Ultra Luminance

UPDATE: 9/10/2018

Installed a new HDMI high speed cable from sound system out to TV from receiver and it fixed the 'no signal' sign when HDR was turned on. Leave HDMI DEEP COLOR ON. (it will pop up the logo) to let you know its working and not a black screen. if you get a black screen somethings wrong with the HDMI. When HDR is working and pops up the logo, go to settings (gear icons in remote), pulls up quick menu and HDR will be highlighted, but say HDR+Standard imaging viewing etc (can be changed). If you're using vivid (my personal choice) when using HDR, set it to HDR+ Vivid. When you do this again, and the TV detects an HDR signal again, it will remember the last HDR+(picture setting) mode you used. (HDR on or OFF) each has thier own image settings.

Random info: if you have a sound system connected to the TV, when using built in TV set apps (You-tube/Hulu etc) you may have to set the receiver/sound system to TV on its remote to get audio coming from the sound system. If you use a Blu-ray players apps, or apps from a game system like PS4 Hulu etc just setting the normal connection input should push the sound like normal.
text_fidelity_b: LG Electronics 70UK6570 70-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV (2018 Model)

text_fidelity_a:
Pogoplug Series 4 Backup Device Pogoplug (this and other models) are an inexpensive way to have some capabilities of more expensive Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices. The most significant difference is a Pogoplug does not come with a hard drive installed. You have to supply your own hard drive as the backup drive. Mostly, I don't recommend this device, or the other offerings in the product line. The Pogoplug is just the beginning of what it will cost to get a complete backup solution with remote access and cloud storage. It's a solution sold piece-by-piece and, in the end, for the same outlay you can buy systems with better functionality and more builtin features.

If all you want is a way to backup files from multiple computers running different Op Systems (e.g. Windows and Mac OS X) to a local backup system, the Pogoplug will do that. If, however, you want to access your files when you're away from home or the office where the Pogoplug is installed, you'll need to buy their app for that from the Pogoplug website.

If you want your files also backed up to cloud storage, you have to buy that as well from the Pogoplug website. They sell 1TB storage, although it's advertised as 'unlimited' cloud storage. In my opinion their cloud storage is expensive. Consider also it takes a very long time to upload 1TB of content and, should you decide to discontinue the service, it takes a lot longer to download that same 1TB.

The best way to think of a Pogoplug is that its like candy dispensing machine. You buy a Pogoplug (the machine) and get one piece of candy free as a promotional item. You purchase more candy one piece at a time. They sell a lot of candy and It's not cheap.

There are some things I like about this item and more I do not. For example, unless you're a big customer, tech support is only available by email. It takes a couple days for a question to turn around and for that and other reasons I don't like email support. Then, too, in order to get all the features I want is an expensive proposition, since the real meaty features cost extra. While Pogoplug Backup (the app that comes with the device) works on both PCs and Macs, it has an annoying glitch on the Mac platform. Whenever a computer restarts (often with all the software updates and service packs) Pogoplug software restarts as well. On the PC, this does not trigger a full backup of already backed up files. On the Mac it does. Essentially, the Pogoplug Backup app for Mac doesn't seem to keep track of what' been backed up so you get to work on a slowed down Mac while Pogoplug needlessly does a full backup. Further, while Pogoplug Backup updates files that have been altered, it does not have versioning.

The most frustrating thing about Pogoplug is that your files are stored on the device locally, on your local network. You'd think it possible to connect directly to the attached drive to access shared files. Not so! Access to files stored on your own drive, located in your own home or office are only available to you from other computers when logged into my.pogoplug.com through their interface. Think how you'll enjoy this when your internet connection is down or their site is down or a myriad other things get fouled up!
text_fidelity_b: Pogoplug Series 4 Backup Device

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black Short story of the review is that these are just as they say they are--a pair of relatively inexpensive "basic" earphones. As such, they seem to be a decent value and have some good points, but if you're looking for sound quality over price, you'll want to go elsewhere.

Pros:
Packaging: small and minimalist as it should be

Provided with: multiple size earbuds caps and ear inserts (more on these later), a very short charging cable, and a decent zip-around traveling pouch

Pairing: No problem with any of my Apple devices. Instantly recognized and paired with an iPhone (8 and 6), iPad (Pro and Air 2), and MacBook Pro. Couldn't be quicker or easier each and every time

Comfort: This was an issue for me, though obviously this is a pretty subjective category. I had to step down immediately to the small caps/rings, which is no surprise--I do that with I think all of my earbuds. But even with the smalls I just couldn't get a a good seal or a comfortable, though oddly enough much worse with my right. The left was not "great" but was certainly good; right was a bad seal and wholly uncomfortable no matter what I tried. Weird.

Sound quality: Again, it's a matter of pricing here. I don't own many basics and it's been years since I've had a set of lower-tier earbuds, so it's hard for me to compare at an equal level. The sound is what I'd call adequate, especially for exercise or listening to an audiobook. But there's no comparison to my PowerBeats3 or Jaybird X2s, and not even to my Jabra Elites, which I"d call my mid-range ones. The first two are in a whole other class in terms of range, sharpness, richness, and comfort, while the Jabras are a good step up in both sound and comfort. Sound here is more than a little thin at both ends, and just not very rich or full. Less noticeable with an audiobook, but definitely not the buds I'd choose if I'm focusing on listening to music, as opposed to having background sound while I"m doing something else. Phone quality is pretty similar--adequate, at times a bit muddy.

Controls: easy, intuitive, and responsive

Overall, if you want a basic set where quality of sound isn't a deal breaker, or a pair of cheaper ones for places you might have to worry about forgetting them, these will suit the bill, assuming you don't have the same comfort issue I did. But for someone looking for rich, full sound, particularly for music, I'd strongly advise moving up the ladder
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Wireless Bluetooth Fitness Headphones Earbuds with Microphone, Black

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System This is the best record cleaning I tried so far. I is very effective in removing dust (and associated static noise) from records that are in reasonably good shape. Of course, it cannot repair records which have been damaged due to being played while dirty. If you acquire a used record in dirty condition, it is probably a good idea to wash it with distilled water first before using the discwasher on it.

I noticed that there are several one-star reviews complaining about the direction of fibers on the cleaning pad that comes with this system. Yes, the cords of the corduroy-like microfiber material does run along the edge of the brush, but this is actually how it should be to provide even coverage across all the grooves. The cords of any fabric is much too thick to fit into the actual grooves on the record. If the cords were to run along the direction of the the grooves, some grooves would be cleaned and some wouldn't. Having the cords being perpendicular to the grooves on the record ensures that all grooves get cleaned evenly. After all, it is the microfibers, not the cords of the fabric, doing the cleaning.

Another advantage of cords running perpendicular to the grooves of the record is that, as you slowly rotate the brush on its axis (as shown in the provided directions), dust that has been collected gets trapped between the cords that are being lifted off the record as the next (clean) cord of the fabric starts making contact with the record surface.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RD1006 Discwasher D4+ Vinyl Record Care System

Wacom Bamboo Pen Tablet After one month of using my Wacom Bamboo Pen which I purchased at Amazon.com I am happy to say that it corrected my repetitive injury (carpal tunnel), and the artwork that I am able to produce now is much closer to the natural form that I am used to in the real world (pencil and paper). I coupled my Wacom pen along with Ubuntu 10.10 and a fantastic application that was developed around the Wacom pen called "MyPaint". I am now very productive in my pursuit as an artist in perfecting my art and I could not be more pleased with this product. For those that wish to try Ubuntu and MyPaint this how you get them...

Since Ubuntu is a free Linux distribution based on the GNU/Linux Debian you can download it free at [...] You can also get the Wacom Bamboo Pen to work by copying and pasting the code below into a terminal within Ubuntu...

sudo add-apt-repository ppa:doctormo/wacom-plus
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install wacom-dkms

Reboot your system and your Wacom Bamboo Pen will be fully functional. Now, to install "MyPaint"...

sudo apt-get install mypaint

No need to reboot after that you will find the application under Applications>Graphics>MyPaint

Enjoy! your Wacom Bamboo Pen. You not only got a great deal from the wonderful people at Amazon.com who sold it to you below the suggested retail price but, if you followed the instructions above and got Ubuntu running on your computer, as well as installing "MyPaint" you have a complete art studio which will serve you well in exploring many things you can achieve using your Wacom Bamboo Pen.

Have a great day! :-)
text_fidelity_b: Wacom Bamboo Pen Tablet

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White) This tablet has entirely streamlined my educational, professional, and personal productivity. I will preface this by saying I chose this tablet (as my very first tablet of any kind) after 5 WEEKS of research and hours and hours of reading the manual, watching video of reviews, unboxing, customization, how-to's, tips and tricks, and specific software guides. I had the nexus 10 in my amazon shopping cart when I first came across this tablet. I will nowhere in this review compare this to an apple device- I have never and will never own one- personal preference, I wholeheartedly believe iOS is sufficient or ideal for a lot of people's use, just not ever going to be for mine. As background, I am in an international DVM program whose laptop just crashed and all 600+gigs of my life were backed up but now only floating in cyberspace so my requirements were a little heady for a tablet-

a) deal with extensive editing and review of PDFs, PPTs, DOCs, XLXS, etc 14-17hrs a day (terms range from 21-24 credits, 4-5hrs of lecture straight, 3-4 hrs of lab with no access to outlet in many labs). Also when I say edit I don't just mean take notes on I also mean incorporate text, figures, etc from textbooks, websites, and other documents.

b) Be a textbook reader and rarely a e-book reader (novels for fun!) Need to access my extensive kindle library, plus some google books and a few Elsevier/pageburst textbooks. Also this needs to be something I am comfortable and accepting of to literally study off of, enough to give up my previous preferring to only study off of paper/actual printed out notes

c) Allow for flawless email, web chat, skype video and text, some web browsing, and file transfer... all on an absolutely horrible school wireless and LAN setup, unpredictable power availability, etc.

d) Streaming and downloading of podcasts, video, MRI, CT, radiographs, and ECG's

e) Be portable to the clinic and the farms for patient-side transcription, recording, etc

f) Get me through the 5-6hr flight and all the airport time!

g) Occasionally watch videos/listen to things for fun

h) Most importantly, due to a dominant hand injury, multiple surgeries, and continued required hand therapy/rehab, I am currently able to write again but not to type with that hand. I therefore wanted a tablet that was stylus intensive- not just for notes, but for navigation, etc. THIS is what made me give up that wonderful squeaky clean android OS of the nexus 10! (I still thing that is probably the best thing for people that want an android tablet but don't NEED a stylus)
So my tablet arrived flawless and flawlessly. The display is beautiful, if anything the screen is too bright- I'm aware my eyes are light sensitive so this won't match with the majority of people but if I do turn my brightness on at all I don't believe I've ever gone above 15%, though I'm sure there will be some case videos poorly and darkly shot that I may need to in the future.

i) at least temporarily, replace my laptop and download and have as much of my backed up laptop files as possible

The tablet was quickly populated with the apps from my HTC phone and google account. The account set up for everything was quick and easy. The initial 2 updates were completed with no adverse signs. Navigation was great, no lag, and I quickly cleared out the stock widgets, set up my panes, and then went into settings.... I activated Developer options and did some customization and disabling there, but most of the disabling I did in app manager, device, and controls. There are very helpful guides out there if you're not sure which apps are safe to disable as well as a "Guide: Longer Battery Life- How You're Being Robbed on XDA that takes you step by step in maximizing your tablet. It was not created at the time when I cleaned up mine but it would've helped greatly!

Here is the gist. The tablet comes crammed full of software and capabilities that I don't need or want. The My Magazine app, a lot of the touchwiz stuff, the eye movement sensors(smart screen), the hand gesture stuff, reading mode, voice control, motions/palm motions, all of that is just a constant battery drain and I will never use them. They were disabled and the vibration feedback for everything was also turned off.

Battery Report: This tablet was shipped within the US twice, and was brought internationally on a plan 4 days later. It was accidently left on the ENTIRE time for about 8 days with six apps up on standby. It arrived with 18% battery left. I use it for 15-17hours a day and end up having to charge it 2-3hrs per about ever 24hr period to get it back to 100. I can use it while it is charging and it will still positively charge during use.

USE FOR A STUDENT: It has replaced textbooks, laptop, printer, scanner, and painstakenly editing and customizing notes and making documents for me. Disclaimer: as someone who used to be able to type 130+ words per minute, I'll make perfectly clear, if you prefer to type and plan on typing a LOT tablet touchscreen keyboards SUCK. This is a fact of life. You can get used to them, you can get proficient at them, but you'll still probably hate it and you're going to need a physical keyboard case/add on if you do a lot of typing of documents or emails. Now, this tablet is made for a stylus. This is not just a peculiarly edged simple piece of plastic that you can buy for just about any touchscreen device and kind of use as a writing device. This is the s-pen, a WACOM and this device and stylus is designed to maximize the experience so you are writing or drawing digitally with an experience just like on paper. Examples- the harder you press the more solid and thicker your pencil/pen/brush/highlighter/calligraphy/etc line. The button on the stylus brings up air command which can be super helpful and it also allows quick screen shots. The stylus allows for fine website navigation that allows you to open drop down windows etc as mouse would. It also offers things a real pen/pencil cant- selective erasing, and selection for drag/drop/copy/paste of ANYTHING to ANYWHERE. You're typing notes and see a great figure and text on a website, you can freehand or rectangular circle what you want and put it into your document. Then you can resize/edit. It's great. I've been using the Snote app for everything thus far, I have made short futile attempts with Lecture Notes and Evernote but I couldn't really get anywhere. I'm not going to give up on then, I just need to research them more to see if I can eventually get them to do what I want and then I can compare them to Snote.

USE FOR A PROFESSIONAL: So far, this has been wonderful. I can seamlessly take notes, look up references, voice record my exam findings, and awkwardly as only a tablet is, take video and pictures of patient's during an exam for later review. (Extremely helpful during lameness and neuro exams for the file). Collaborative documents through Polaris office and google drive is exceptional- as fast as a laptop and more portable, and better screen size than a smartphone. It runs better than the school computers for running presentations off of onto projectors. I can also have students I tutor digitally sign- literally our weekly sheets and submit them via email with one step- completely negating the awesome printer and scanner I brought down here.

USE FOR A CONSUMER: I find this tablet beautiful for watching movies and videos and the sound is great. In a classroom of 50 people chatting between classes I have no problem hearing the speakers among the hub but there are completely valid reports that even cranked the sound might get lost a little if you're in a very loud close crowd. Sound improves with earbuds but the initial audio set up app (basically a hearing test and then a customized audio scheme for you) was startling when it compared the stock/base line settings to what it came up with for ME.

USE FOR AN ARTIST: I'm still learning and adapting, I'll never turn to this instead of actual physical art supplies and paper but it is fun and I can really see myself doing more digital than before. It has been especially nice for graphic design, photoshopping, etc.

USE AS A LEFTY: no issues except see below for one thing that affects both right and left handers...

ISSUES: 1) One day after about a week of ownership, my battery was in the upper 80's, I was taking some notes and about 2hrs later I looked at the status bar and it was 29%. I went into Battery in Settings, and the s-pen interface was responsible for 80% of the battery use. I shut down and then restarted and it's never happened again. Similarly the Android OS did the same thing at a later instance but again it was a one time thing and in both cases the battery recharged speedily after and stayed charged.
2) Snote- I have had weird episodes where an import fails, or it force closes itself repeatedly when I try to rename or change the cover of one particular document. After this erratic behavior occurred twice in three days and completely clearing and restarting Snote from scratch (everything backed up and replaced on my Samsung account) to no avail, I did a factory reset. The last ¾ of my ownership have seen no such problems any more. I will warn you that if you wipe out S note and you start from scratch in it and re-transfer all your SNote files back in, if you have a lot of really big files, it can take a really long time to re-populate.
3) The menu/return and physical home button- occasionally based on the desk I'm at, if my arm isn't supported and my wrist is resting fully on the edge of the tablet, these buttons will get pressed while I'm writing. Its purely an annoyance and doesn't affect the writing or do anything but I definitely have to reposition if I find I'm getting lazy on holding my wrist up at these desks.

Wrap up: I only use in landscape, it's just like writing on a portrait piece of paper except you can also zoom. I got used to writing on the tablet and the tiny stylus very quickly but there are compatible Samsung styli of various widths and sizes out there as well. I thought about waiting for the new 12.2 whose screen is literally a full piece of paper landscape, but I realized this is perfect for me and more portable than the 12.2 will be (this thing can just squeeze into one of the pockets on one of my lab coats. I was planning on having to use the Nova launcher to avoid any lag but truly, this tablet was a speed demon already and I eventually got Nova solely for the customization ability and cleaner interface. It allows me to avoid more things I don't use and I didn't lose ANY of the software I do.

Bottom line, RESEARCH! PREPARE! And there will STILL BE A LEARNING CURVE! But it will be based on discovering unexpected cool features instead of on frustration). If you won't heavily use the stylus, don't spend the money on this tablet. If you're just curious if you could "get into a stylus" try one out first but prepare first so you can use it to the full advantage while you're there. Also, I came from NO tablet and no Samsung/Note experience and there are changes between the previous model and this. You don't actually lose much but things are moved around and different. Don't be scared to optimize it, I'm not talking rooting, though adventurous forays into that terrain have finally arrived as well. In conclusion I love it, it has made things so much more efficient for me, I get a lot DONE with it and it's basically all I have to carry around. I purchased the 32gig tablet plus a 64gig Sandisk XC which installed and worked like a charm. There are annoyances that come up but any issue I have had I have been able to fix. I have everything safely backed up on Carbonite and there's a million ways to sync all of your accounts if you chose (note some of this may be unnecessary or frequency can be dialed back too)

It performs and looks beautiful and I am still learning.

EDIT: FLASH PLAYER: This tablet absolutely supports flash. Youtube and embedded flash worked right out of the box, however, to watch my amazon video's etc, I just downloaded the following file- I cannot post the actual link but it's a drop box file. Install this and make sure flash is enabled in your browser settings/plugins and it will work in the stock browser, Dolphin, and Mozilla. Some people also recommend having your browser set to View Desktop site.

Edit 12/15/2014: Please see my comment under product question- "Can you use amazon prime video on the galaxy 10.1 2014 ed? asked by Judith C. Love on November 14, 2013" for instructions and the direct link for flash file

Edit 02/2017: My tablet got slammed by careless sleep-deprived brain addled 4th year vet students and the screen got shattered in the upper right corner. Still useable, not any real issues but concern about the little chips and cracks gradually loosening and only being held together by the screen protector I was itching to replace due to scratches but now couldnt, left me with the desire to replace as I was 4 months out of my extended warranty. Call it coincidence but literally as I powered up the replacement, this original tablet FAILED. The screen doesn't illuminate. At certain angle/light you can see it's on but there is no way for me to see well enough to unlock the screen and at least access over 3 years of my life on the original tablet. I am 99% convinced this is secondary to the trauma/screen break, and I had nearly everything backed up via Carbonite on the original except for the past few months of random downloads. Still, I am grieved and wanted a moment of silence.

Yes we had great times together but I am truly sad and a bit devastated because the replacement came with OS updates that I had been actively refusing to install for the past year. Thus, my new tablet in short, I can't stand. It's the same make and model except offers 4G which I don't use but it is unbearably slow (cant load my pdf vet school notes worth a damn- it's faster for me to find a computer, login to carbonite back up, download the enormous file and open it on the computer than to scroll through the pdf on the tablet one page per 10 seconds loading. It's truly unbearable. All the updates and changes are awful and its so slow despite me instantly ditching touchwhiz and using Nova Launcher.

Moment of silence for my beloved original, maybe one day science will advance enough for me to communicate with you without a working screen so that I can have you back. Laughingly, the one OS update I did do that slowed you down, turns out, compared to the ones that followed, you were still almost the speed of light comparatively.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Note 10.1 2014 Edition (32GB, White)

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling I've had the opportunity to review three different G.G. Martinsen players, and of the three this one is my favorite. I brought two of the players, pre-charged, to review at my sister's where I am staying a week while she had and recovers from surgery, and the one thing I can say right off the bat is that I wish the charging cable was of the ubiquitous Micro-A type and not the mini type, which I did not think to bring with me. The [[ASIN:B016F4AGLC other player]] handles like the [[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ first one]] I reviewed for G.G. Martinsen, but I will have to wait until I get back home to do anything other than test the recorder and FM radio on this 16GB player because I have no cable to copy music onto the player with!

Anyway, unlike the other two players, the controls on this one make sense and handle more like what I'm used to. The instructions that come with this (that I also left at home!) were well-written in English, unlike so many products coming out of China these days. But I haven't needed the instructions to figure out how to use this player or change the settings. The first thing I did was set the Power Off and Sleep settings to 0 so the player won't shut off unless I flip the manual switch to turn it off. I have been listening to this player while I've been writing reviews, and I have had absolutely no cutouts with the FM radio even though I'm in a condo sandwiched on all sides by other units and this place is bad with reception of cable TV and other radios. I like that the station stays selected even when you power the player off and on again.

The control dial is easy to see, with a top Menu button, left and right arrows, and a pause/play button on the bottom (something the other players did not have). The round button in the middle has a good tactile feel, and even in the dark it's fairly easy to feel where to press for the different functions. I'll have to re-read the instructions to understand fully when to use the center button and how.

The little piece you can thread a lanyard into is plastic, but I don't think it will break easily unless you put a lot of stress on it. The player comes with a pair of original Apple-style earphones, which are great for walking outside where you need to be able to hear sounds around you while listening to music. The headphones are not the best in the world, but they are a nice additional feature and good to have in situations where you wouldn't want pricier headphones to get ruined (the gym, outside should it start raining). Of course, your listening experience will only be as good as the wired headphones you plug into this player. It really is a whole lot of bang for the buck and an attractive little player. I have the turquoise color, and it's really nice.

I put links to the other two players I have reviewed so you can compare them. What I like about this one is it doesn't have that gimmicky bubble-gum type selection screen but, rather, just has a list of the different features and functions. The list is easy to read and looks more businesslike and professional than the more cartoonish screens of the other two players.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling

text_fidelity_a:
Onkyo HT-S3500 660 Watt 5.1-Channel Home Theater Speaker/Receiver Package This system ROCKS! We got it for our Roku, and aside from a few slight annoyances with the setup, it works and sounds awesome. It works very well for our living room and my wife can now hear the movies instead of asking me what they said all the time. I would like to point out for some people that the HDMI output to the TV is only for the HDMI inputs and not "One port to rule them all". If you use a component device with the red, blue and green plugs (us: older DVD player) you need to have a set run from component out to the component in on the TV. Same goes with the RCA style (red, yellow, white) to get video on that. I was very disappointed that I couldn't just run one HDMI to the TV and be done with it.

Secondly the unit gets warm. I mean very warm and electronic smelly. I read the other reviews and I also experienced a similar issue. So after a week, I grabbed an unused 120mm computer fan and a old router power supply and made a cooling fan that rests on the top of the head unit. It helped a ton. I no longer smell anything, and the whole thing is now cool to the tough. I control the power to the fan using one of those green power strips that turns off stuff. Others used a USB fan from the iPod port on the unit. I do recommend that you cool this somehow to increase its lifespan.

The speaker wire that came with the system is junk and too short for my purposes. I ordered some thicker gauge wire [[ASIN:B0029HHIDY RCA AH16100SN 100 Ft. 16-Gauge Speaker Wire]]for my needs. The sounds is great with this better/bigger wire and I could put it where I wanted.

So these maybe deal breakers for some, but the price was right and we live with the other issues, but since this unit works so well, it seems like a small price to pay for good sound. Overall I highly recommend this unit.
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo HT-S3500 660 Watt 5.1-Channel Home Theater Speaker/Receiver Package

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz Delta Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones w/Microphone in Ear Bass All Metal Buds (OldSNM) This is one of those earphones where nearly every piece of praise has to be qualified with “for the price.” But that’s not a bad thing. I like and appreciate high-end earphones but I won’t take a pricey set with me to the gym since there’s a good chance it will get broken or lost. At the same time, I don’t want to listen to the rough sound that the $10 or so buds produce.

This is a great compromise. They sound far better than you would expect give the price but they are no so pricey that it would be a tragedy if they get dropped and mashed by a treadmill (which has happened to me), dropped in the pool (also happened to me) or left behind/stolen (fortunately, not happened to me as of yet).

The build quality is pretty good for the price. The cables are on the thin side, but well-anchored. The 3.5mm plug is angled which makes it easier to plug in, and also keeps it from sticking out too much on an mp3 player. It does not come with a case or any extras other than a set of various sizes of tips.

Comfort is a feature that does not have to be qualified by price – these fit very well and are so lightweight that I don’t even notice that they are on. The set includes a variety of tips to customize the fit to your ear. Since bass response is partially dependent on a good ear fit, you’ll want to experiment with the various sizes of tips to see which offer the best feel and bass response.

The sound clarity is quite good at low to mid volumes. They get rather harsh at louder volumes – these are not earbuds that like to get pushed much beyond a middle of the road volume setting. But while they are in their comfort zone in terms of volume, the sound is clear. The bass response won't shake your skull, but it's decent. Sound isolation is also pretty good.

These won’t thrill you with superlative sound, elegant design or impressive looks, but their performance and build quality are impressive for the price point, and much better than the typical low-end earbuds. Well worth considering if you’re looking for an inexpensive pair of earphones.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz Delta Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones w/Microphone in Ear Bass All Metal Buds (OldSNM)

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver I returned these because of a software bug with ANC - and also because the call quality was terrible.

These phones stood out for being wireless with active noise cancellation (ANC) AND pass through (so you can hear ambient sounds for safety in the City). Unfortunately, those features are the weak points of the headphones - to the point that I found I would never use the pass through and often didn't bother with the ANC.

SOUND QUALITY: VERY GOOD - EXCEPT - they tend to exaggerate the mid base a little which can make vocals - especially male vocals sound a little unclear. Listening to the same music on speakers vs the headphones, it was just plane more real sounding and pleasant on good speakers. High standard, I know. Other headphones don't have that particular problem (though may have others - like weak bass or sibilant highs). I haven't heard that many competing models, so I don't know how they compare to sennheiser or bose or anyone else in the same price class. At least others have an app with equalization (Jabra, Jaybird).

Bug w. ANC: Sometimes it would say it's on when it's off and vice-versa.

ANNOYING THING: When you engage the pass-through, it has a voice prompt that tells you the pass through is engaged. Since often I switch on the pass through when it's important to hear something, the several seconds it takes to make its silly announcement means I miss part of what I was trying to hear! I found I would always just yank one plug out of my ear instead and get the instant feedback. ALSO - this thing takes FOREVER to turn off. You have to hold hold hold and finally it announces it's powering off. Combined with poor power indicator light - this is just annoying.

NOTE: This is not a defect, but just poor design... There is NO WAY to activate Google Assistant or Siri with These. Even my cheapo earbuds let you use one of the buttons to summon Google. Without that, how are you supposed to make voice calls? I have to pull out my phone to make calls. Foo.

Combined with atrocious call quality (I could hear them, but the person on the other end is always mishearing words or saying WHAT? WHAT?), these are DOA for me.

ONE LAST THING: The APP is garbage. Just pointless.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Dual Driver BT ANC In-Ear Headphones Wireless Bluetooth Earphones with Active Noise Cancellation, ENC, Fast Charging, Magnetic Earbuds, Microphone and Volume Controls, Silver

Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold) This folding keyboard is a bit of a betwixt and between product, but if it is the sort of thing you think you might use, then it’s got a lot to like about it. If you have a tablet (and my experience is with iPads so keep that in mind), then their built in keyboard is a better choice for short work just because it’s larger and more natural to type. For longer work, the choice will be more individual in that some people hate writing for extended time on the hard surface of a tablet keyboard and others don’t mind at all. I can do a pretty long stint and for really long work, I’ll shift over to a Bluetooth keyboard, either Apple’s own or a smaller Logitech one that also acts as a cover. I’d prefer both of those to this because again, they are larger and so more comfortable.

When one considers the keyboard as a phone accessory, then things change a bit, and this become a much more viable choice. If I have to do any halfway extensive typing on a phone for work (something beyond texting, an email or two, etc., then this would definitely be my preference over the phone itself.

1) it takes up very little space (and comes with a nice little pouch). Tossing it into a backpack is nothing, but I could easily fit it into a coat pocket, a cargo pants-like pocket, keep it in my car console without it blocking much space. None of which would be true for my wireless Apple keyboard or even my slimmer Logitech one. The additional “bulk” is therefore relatively negligible.

2) the typing is quite nice on it. I was pleasantly surprised at the key travel, the ease, the tactile sense.

3) It’s definitely small and a little cramped, but not so I notice it unless I’m typing for a long time (half hour or more) and then I just need to take a few minutes break. The small size doesn’t come into play too often. I had to readjust to the apostrophe, and one has to hunt and seek a bit for less-used keys, but that’s easy enough and once you’ve been typing for a while it becomes just as second nature as normal typing does. And it’s much faster and much more comfortable than extensive phone typing

4) the stand is a nice little touch that works quite well, placing the phone at a usable and pleasant working angle and letting you sue it in both portrait and landscape mode.

5) I haven’t exhausted the battery so can’t speak to how long it will go, but it’s certainly lasted a good number of hours, more than I’d ever use it for (if I’m working that long I’m going to my laptop or tablet)

6). Build quality seems sufficient. I wouldn’t say it feels highly durable, but nor would I call it cheap feeling or overly flimsy. And when it’s folded I have no concerns about it breaking.

All in all this was actually quite the pleasant surprise and again, if you would ever find yourself needing to use your phone for that sort of mid-range work (more than you’d want to do on a phone keyboard but not so much you’re turning to a laptop) then I’d highly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold)

1. These headphones are really different in appearance from regular earbud-type headphones, but they are oddly attractive in their design.

2. They are great for swimming in a pool or in any outdoor body of water, because they are extensively waterproof. They can be submerged to a depth of 20 meters (65 feet). This means they can be used for snorkeling and scuba diving.

6. This type of headphones are outstanding for safety purposes. People who walk, jog or run on public sidewalks or, especially, on deserted park paths/trails, are taking a big risk if they have their ears plugged with regular Bluetooth earbuds such that are not aware of sounds around them that could signal danger (e.g., a bike speeding down the park trail, careless skaters or skateboarders sharing the sidewalk and, worst of all, muggers).

6. A built-in microphone allows you to use the Bluetooth function to place and received calls on your cell phone.

7. These headphones are lightweight, durable, and flexible.

CONS

1. Other than for water sports and for safety purposes, these headphones are not as good as regular earbuds, because their sound quality is comparatively quite inferior.

2. Compared to regular Bluetooth earbuds, their price is very high.

Donner Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.2 Earphones with 4 Mic Clear Calls, 12mm Drivers, App for Custom EQ, 32H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency - Dobuds ONE, Blue Budget-priced earbuds are complicated to review because, in my experience, all $200 earbuds sound significantly better than all $50 earbuds, but there is still a lot of demand for value-priced "good enough" products. I do own a couple of $200 earbuds and they do sound noticeably richer and clearer than these $40 earbuds. However, when I'm out jogging or traveling (eg airplane or train) or listening to voice podcasts, having the absolute best sound quality isn't really important to me. In those situations, features are more important to me, like active noise cancellation, equalization, good volume, good battery life, and easy access to the features. I'd rather use cheap earbuds that I don't mind losing somewhere along the way.

These earbuds have average quality sound for the $40 price. Where these Donner earbuds beat the competition is the features. I've never owned $40 earbuds with app control before. The user manual has a QR code to let you download the app. The QR code did not work, but I did find the "Donner Control" app in the Google Play app store and the app works fine on my Android phone. The app lets me pick from pre-programmed equalization settings or design my own. Adjusting the equalization for different types of music makes a significant difference in audio clarity. The app also lets me choose from 3 active noise cancellation modes. These features don't work as well as in $200 earbuds, but these are $40 earbuds and most $40 earbuds don't have any of these features or any app at all. You can control some of these features with the confusing set of triple-tap commands on the earbuds, but I can never remember those and would rather just tap the picture in the app.

The app also lets you download firmware updates from Donner. None was available when I checked, but this could be a great way for them to refine the features of the earbuds or even add new features. They ask you to give them your email address and create an account when you open the app, but I did not and the core features of the app still work OK.

Battery life for these earbuds is good for this price range (6 to 8 hours, depending on whether or not you use ANC). As with most budget-priced wireless earbuds, maximum volume is OK but not great. Bass is above average for the $40 price. Static noise is very low. The Bluetooth connection has been very stable for me, even when I'm 30 feet away from my phone or in a different room in the house.

I can't give these earbuds 5 stars because I can easily buy better sound quality with more money, but these are solid 4 stars for value at the current $40 price.
text_fidelity_b: Donner Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.2 Earphones with 4 Mic Clear Calls, 12mm Drivers, App for Custom EQ, 32H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency - Dobuds ONE, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech HD Webcam C525, Portable HD 720p Video Calling with Autofocus - Black [[VIDEOID:132a9e1a9608d7ddcfd6e870320f72aa]] The 75 second video is intended as a supplement to the written review so that you can see for yourself how well my fairly standard computer can record 720p, and thus get an idea if your computer can benefit from a 720p recording device. This is important to consider because even the manufacturer mentions that many computers cannot keep up with the recording. I mention my system specs in the video.

It's a well designed webcam. It is very small, and the ability to protect its own lens is great. They supply ~5 ft. cord that - wrapped up - takes up about as much room as the camera itself, which allows a connection between a desktop and a separate monitor. Better would have been if they used a standard micro USB connector or some kind of cord wrap system to keep all that out of your way and allow you to use a 30cm cord for connection to your laptop.

The actual optics seem great and the autofocus works pretty well. Even Win XP SP2 allowed me to use the camera function (no video) immediately without installing any software. The software that comes with it eats up nearly 300MB of ROM (that includes their own calling application and editing software that you don't need to install) and only tries caducously to take over your computer (a registry edit and startup menu delete gets rid of unwanted reminders and useless junk running in the background). Oh...I noticed one typo in their software, which is unacceptable, and it also keeps telling me that it doesn't recognize the mic (which is built into the camera), but it records sound anyway.

The design allows for mounting on a monitor 26mm thick or less, but I suppose you could sort of lay it on top of a CRT monitor with no problems. It also allows for a fairly stable mounting on a laptop.

Great device that I would recommend, but I had to take off a star for less than perfect portability and some software blips.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Webcam C525, Portable HD 720p Video Calling with Autofocus - Black

text_fidelity_a: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop First let me say that I grew up typing on actual typewriters and I find myself getting really nostalgic about those days the older I get.  Not that I mind sleek, modern keyboards.  I do a great deal of writing, so I have adapted to the various styles as they've come out.  This particular keyboard is nice and pleasant to work on, but I wouldn't say it's a true typewriter style experience.  The keys are too flat and too round for that.  If you are like me and you do a lot of typing and can adapt yourself quickly between different keyboards you will probably enjoy this one.  I do find myself making a lot of typos that I normally wouldn't when I'm working on it though.  The mouse is honestly just annoying.  There is no actual switch to turn it off, just a button right on top that seems to 'wake' it when it goes dormant, so if you're prone to bumping it around or accidentally dropping things on it or if you plan on using it in multiple places for any reason whatsoever you will find yourself getting frustrated with just how easy it is to turn it back on.  The scroll wheel is fantastic, but the one on my previous mouse no longer works at all, so that might be the reason why I like it so much.  The accuracy of its tracking leaves a lot to be desired and it's quite loud when you click it, but I do tend to prefer to keep my environment quiet.  All in all I would not purchase this again both because the keyboard design is just 'off' in enough nit-picky ways to make it frustrating (so many typos) and because the mouse tracking and lack of a true 'off' switch makes it frustrating to actually use it.  Both the keyboard and the mouse are really pretty to look at and well built for what they are, but I wouldn't call them truly functional even though they do work.  If you're just doing minor browsing and not a lot of typing they would be fine for that, but if you're someone that does a lot of writing or anything that requires precision tracking of the mouse like playing games or working in paint programs you should probably skip this set.
text_fidelity_b: Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo, Black Colorful Retro 2.4GHz Typewriter with Cute Round Keycaps, DPI Adjustable Optical Compatible PC Laptop
